metadata.name: [GCP Compute OTel] Clustered VM interruptions in a zone
metadata.description: Alerts when at least 3 distinct VMs in the same zone record an interruption (live-migration maintenance event, Spot/preemptible preemption, or host-error termination) within 30 minutes. Single maintenance events are expected background noise and do not alert. Returns one row per affected project and zone.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.compute.otel-*
// Compute Engine VM instances only
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
    AND attributes.interruption_type IS NOT NULL
    AND attributes.interruption_type != "none"
// interruption_count is a GAUGE: 1 (or more) in the minute an interruption occurred, otherwise 0 or absent.
| STATS events = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/interruption_count`))
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone, resource.attributes.instance_id, attributes.instance_name, attributes.interruption_type
| WHERE events > 0
// Optional: restrict to a type, for example | WHERE attributes.interruption_type == "MaintenanceEvent"
| STATS
    interrupted_instances = COUNT_DISTINCT(resource.attributes.instance_id),
    interruption_types = VALUES(attributes.interruption_type),
    interrupted_instance_names = VALUES(attributes.instance_name)
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone

breach.segment:
// Breach: 3 or more distinct VMs interrupted in the zone within the window. Raise for large fleets.
WHERE interrupted_instances >= 3
| KEEP resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone, interrupted_instances, interruption_types, interrupted_instance_names
| SORT interrupted_instances DESC
| LIMIT 50

data.content:
## Clustered VM interruptions in a zone

Several VMs in this zone were interrupted within 30 minutes, by live migration for host maintenance (`MaintenanceEvent`), by Spot/preemptible reclamation (`PreemptionEvent`), or by a host error that terminated the VM (`TerminationEvent`). One-off maintenance events are normal; a cluster points to a GCE maintenance wave, a capacity crunch for Spot VMs, failing hosts, or a zone-level infrastructure event.

### Triage
1. Check `interruption_types`. A `PreemptionEvent` cluster means Spot capacity is being reclaimed; expect more to follow. `TerminationEvent` means VMs were stopped by host errors: check that they restarted (automatic restart policy).
2. Check whether the interrupted VMs share a workload (for example one instance group) and whether that service degraded.
3. Check CPU steal and disk latency on the interrupted VMs around the event time: live migration can cause brief performance dips.
4. Check the Google Cloud status dashboard for the zone.

### Remediation
For Spot preemptions, make sure workloads tolerate termination or shift capacity to on-demand or another zone. For maintenance waves, verify instance availability policies (`onHostMaintenance`) and that services spread replicas across zones.

### Tuning
Adjust `interrupted_instances >= 3` relative to the fleet size per zone, or filter on `interruption_type`. The 30-minute window controls how long the alert stays active after the cluster. GCP Cloud Monitoring metrics typically arrive several minutes late, so the most recent minutes of the lookback window may be empty; the window is sized to tolerate this.
